Prevention: Undertake crop rotation with rice, maize, sorghum and pearl millet.
Early sowing before 30-45 days before normal date of sowing.
Follow good field sanitation practices such as sufficient irrigation, as over- irrigating can increase the risk of spreading the bacteria.
Monitoring: Young plants remain with green leaves which leads to sudden wilting and death.
In mature plants leaves turn to light green with curling at the tip.
Dip the root in water to notice bacterial ooze coming from the cut end.
Dying branches often curl to form a "shepherd's crook".
Consider direct control actions as soon as symptoms are found on crops.
Direct Control: Collect and destroy infected plant parts by burning.
Pseudomonas fluorescens at a rate of 1 kg per acre.
Bacillus subtillus at a rate of 800 g per acre.
Restrictions: Always use precautionary wearing of goggles and protective clothing.
Bacterimycin, Bactrinashak) (immunomodulators) at a rate of 60 g per acre.
